'''Samuel James Patterson''' (September 7, 1948 in Belfast)<ref name=profile>[https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=ai:patterson.samuel-james Author Profile: Samuel James Patterson] in [[Zentralblatt MATH|zbMATH database]]</ref> is a [[Northern Irish]] mathematician specializing in [[analytic number theory]].  He has been a professor at the [[University of Göttingen]] since 1981.<ref name=natlib>[https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=idn%3D113779127 Literature by and about Samuel J. Patterson] in the [[German National Library]] catalogue</ref>

==Biography==
Patterson was born in Belfast and grew up in the east of the city, attending [[Grosvenor High School]].{{fact|date=November 2025}} He went to [[Clare College, Cambridge]], in 1967, and received his BA in mathematics in 1970, and his Ph.D. (completed in 1974, awarded in 1975) on "The limit set of a Fuchsian group" under [[Alan Beardon]].<ref name=acta>{{cite journal
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| title=The limit set of a Fuchsian group
| journal=Acta Mathematica
| volume=136
| date=1976
| pages=241–273
| doi=10.1007/BF02392046 | doi-access=free}}</ref>  He spent 1974–1975 at Göttingen, 1975–1979 he was back at Cambridge, and 1979–1981 he was at Harvard as [[Benjamin Peirce#Eponyms|Benjamin Pierce Lecturer]]. From 1981 to his retirement in 2011 he was professor of mathematics at Göttingen.

His 18 PhD students include {{ill|Jörg Brüdern|de|vertical-align=sup}} and Bernd Otto Stratmann.<ref name=mathgene>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=25294 Samuel James Patterson] at the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref>{{dead|date=November 2025}}

He is the brother of the Northern Irish taxonomist [[David Joseph Patterson]].{{fact|date=November 2025}}

==Mathematics==
Subjects that Patterson deals with include discontinuous groups ([[Fuchsian group]]s), different [[zeta function]]s (for example those of [[David Ruelle|Ruelle]] and [[Atle Selberg|Selberg]], in particular those associated with certain groups of infinite covolume<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| title=The Laplacian operator on a Riemann surface
| journal=Compositio Mathematica
| volume=31
| issue=1
| pages=83–107
| date=1975
| url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=CM_1975__31_1_83_0}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| title=The Laplacian operator on a Riemann surface II
| journal=Compositio Mathematica
| volume=32
| issue=1
| pages=71–112
| date=1976
| url=http://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1976__32_1_71_0}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| title=The Laplacian operator on a Riemann surface III
| journal=Compositio Mathematica
| volume=33
| issue=3
| pages=227–259
| date=1976
| url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=CM_1976__33_3_227_0}}</ref><ref>{{cite conference
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| title=The Selberg zeta-function of a Kleinian group
| book-title=Number theory, trace formulas and discrete groups
| conference=Symposium in Honor of Atle Selberg, Oslo/Norway 1987
| pages=409–441
| date=1989
| doi=10.1016/B978-0-12-067570-8.50031-7}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| last2=Perry | first2=Peter A.
| title=The divisor of Selberg's zeta function for Kleinian groups
| journal=Duke Mathematical Journal
| volume=106
| issue=2
| pages=321–390
| date=2001
| doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-01-10624-8}}</ref>), [[metaplectic group]]s,<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Kazhdan | first1=D. A. | authorlink1=David Kazhdan
| last2=Patterson | first2=S. J.
| title=Metaplectic forms
| journal=[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]]
| volume=59
| issue=310
| year=1984
| pages=35–142
| mr= 
| url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=PMIHES_1984__59__35_0
| doi=10.1007/BF02698770| s2cid=189782518 | url-access=subscription
}}</ref> generalized [[theta function]]s, and [[exponential sum]]s in analytical number theory.

In 1978, together with [[Roger Heath-Brown]], he disproved the [[Kummer sum#Patterson's conjecture|Kummer conjecture on cubic Gauss sums]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Heath-Brown | first1= D. Roger | authorlink1=Roger Heath-Brown
| last2=Patterson | first2=S. J.
| title=The distribution of Kummer sums at prime arguments
| journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]
| volume=1979
| issue=310
| year=1979
| pages= 111–130
| mr=0546667
| doi= 10.1515/crll.1979.310.111| s2cid= 122636972 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| mr=1815372
| last=Heath-Brown
| first=D. R.
| authorlink1=Roger Heath-Brown
| title=Kummer's conjecture for cubic Gauss sums
| journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume=120
| issue=1
| year=2000
| pages=97–124
| url=http://eprints.maths.ox.ac.uk/archive/00000158/01/kummer.pdf
| doi=10.1007/s11856-000-1273-y
| doi-access=
| s2cid=16144134
}}{{Dead link|date=May 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

He proposed a new conjecture<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| title=On the distribution of Kummer sums
| journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]
| volume=1978
| issue=303/304
| pages=126–143
| date=1978
| doi=10.1515/crll.1978.303-304.126| s2cid=116200023
}}</ref> which was based on insights from his determination of the coefficients of the cuspidal Fourier expansions of the metaplectic cubic theta function.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| title=A cubic analogue of the theta series
| journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]
| volume=1977
| issue=296
| pages=125–161
| date=1977
| doi=10.1515/crll.1977.296.125| s2cid=201060648
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Patterson | first1=S. J.
| title=A cubic analogue of the theta series II
| journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]
| volume=1977
| issue=296
| pages=217–220
| date=1977
| doi=10.1515/crll.1977.296.217| s2cid=115916674
}}</ref> This revised conjecture remained open until 2021, when it was finally proved by Alexander Dunn and Maksym Radziwiłł at Caltech.<ref>[https://www.iflscience.com/after-175-years-two-false-conjectures-and-the-birth-of-computing-this-theorem-finally-has-a-proof-65065 After 175 Years, Theorem Finally Has a Proof] by Katie Spalding, [[IFLScience]], Aug 26, 2022</ref><ref>[https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-numerical-mystery-from-the-19th-century-finally-gets-solved-20220815 A Numerical Mystery From the 19th Century Finally Gets Solved] by  Leila Sloman, [[Quanta Magazine]], August 15, 2022</ref>

In 1976 Patterson introduced what later became known as the Patterson-Sullivan measure.<ref name="acta"/> The concept was further developed and extended by [[Dennis Sullivan]] starting in 1979.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Sullivan | first1=Dennis | authorlink1=Dennis Sullivan
| title=The density at infinity of a discrete group of hyperbolic motions
| journal=[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]]
| volume=50
| date=1979
| pages=171–202
| doi=10.1007/BF02684773| s2cid=10566772 | url=http://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1979__50__171_0/ | url-access=subscription
}}</ref> It has proved to be a useful tool in studying [[Fuchsian group|Fuchsian]] and [[Kleinian group]]s (and certain generalizations) and their limit sets.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Sullivan | first1=Dennis | authorlink1=Dennis Sullivan
| title=Entropy, Hausdorff measures old and new, and limit sets of geometrically finite Kleinian groups
| journal=Acta Mathematica
| volume=153
| date=1984
| pages=259–277
| doi=10.1007/BF02392379 | doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book
| last1=Nicholls | first1=Peter J.
| title=The ergodic theory of discrete groups
| series=LMS Lecture Note Series
| volume=143
| date=1989
| doi=10.1017/CBO9780511600678| isbn=9780521376747
}}</ref>

==History of mathematics==
Patterson is also interested in the [[history of mathematics]]. For example, together with Ralf Meyer, he contributed an updated introduction to a new edition of a classic textbook by [[Hermann Weyl]],<ref name=birthday1/> and an introduction to the classic textbook of Whittaker and Watson.<ref>E.T. Whittaker and G.N. Watson: Modern Analysis, 5th  Edition, (Edited and prepared for publication by Victor H. Moll), 2021.</ref>  He has collaborated with [[Norbert Schappacher]] on elucidating the biography of [[Kurt Heegner]].

==Honors and awards==
In 1984 Patterson received the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners#Whead%20List%20of%20LMS%20prize%20winners%5D%20The%20London%20Mathematical%20Society List of LMS prize winners] The London Mathematical Society</ref>  He is on the executive committee of the Leibniz Archives based in [[Hannover]]<ref>[https://www.gwlb.de/Leibniz/Leibnizarchiv/english/introduction/ Leibniz-Archiv/Leibniz Research Center] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200322070351/http://www.gwlb.de/Leibniz/Leibnizarchiv/english/introduction/ |date=22 March 2020 }} [[Hannover]]</ref> and has been a member of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences]] since 1998.<ref>[https://adw-goe.de/mitglieder/personendetails/person/samuel-james-patterson/ Göttingen Academy of Sciences: member Samuel James Patterson]</ref> From 1982 to 1994 he was an editor of [[Crelle's Journal]].<ref>{{cite journal
| title=Frontmatter
| journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]
| volume=2018
| date=April 2018
| issue=737
| pages=i-iv
| doi=10.1515/crelle-2018-frontmatter737 | doi-access=free}}</ref>

To mark his 60th birthday friends and colleagues in Göttingen organized a three-day conference to celebrate his life in July, 2009.<ref name=birthday1>[https://www.uni-math.gwdg.de/patterson/ International Conference on the Occasion of the 60th Birthday of Samuel J. Patterson] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180919092044/http://www.uni-math.gwdg.de/patterson/ |date=19 September 2018 }} Göttingen, July 27–29, 2009</ref> Speakers at this gathering included [[Daniel Bump]], [[Dorian Goldfeld]], 
[[David Kazhdan]], and [[Andrew Ranicki]].<ref name=birthday2>[http://www.uni-goettingen.de/de/3240.html?archive=true&archive_source=presse&archive_id=3318 Mathematics: International Conference on Questions of Number Theory] [[University of Göttingen]]</ref> A commemorative volume, ''Contributions in Analytic and Algebraic Number Theory'' (Springer 2012), edited by Valentin Blomer & [[Preda Mihăilescu]], collecting articles related to or developed at the conference, was issued as a [[Festschrift]] for him.<ref name=comem>[https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9781461412182 Festschrift for S. J. Patterson] The text that comprises this volume is a collection of surveys and original works from experts in the fields of algebraic number theory, analytic number theory, harmonic analysis, and hyperbolic geometry. A portion of the collected contributions have been developed from lectures given at the "International Conference on the Occasion of the 60th Birthday of S. J. Patterson"</ref>
